title: Staged runtime dependency shepherding — upgrade plan (draft)
summary: Draft plan for coordinating dependent component upgrades across on-prem/VPC private deployments. Focuses on dependency ownership, terraform module sequencing, API/CRD compatibility gates, canary patterns, fallbacks, and rehearsal checklist.
content:
Context:
This is a working draft for how we shepherd upgrades that touch multiple subsystems in private deployments: runtime binaries, control-plane components, operator CRDs, and the terraform modules that provision heterogeneous on-prem hardware. The goal is minimal customer disruption and deterministic rollback paths.
notes: High-level approach: assign a single dependency shepherd for each upstream dependency (runtime, operator, tf modules, image registry), declare compatibility gates, run a rehearsal in the lab cluster, then do phased customer rollouts. Keep the control plane and runtime compatibility surface mapped explicitly (CRDs, API fields, kv schema).
steps:
1) Preflight inventory (owner: Ravi) -- map all customers in scope, catalog runtime versions, operator versions, tf module versions, kernel/cuda stacks, and any custom patches. Export CSV and attach in Jira.

2) Compatibility matrix (owner: Maya) -- produce a matrix: runtime X control-plane X operator X tf-module. Mark safe combos, combos requiring migration shims, and blocked combos. Use the matrix to derive allowed canary set.

3) Terraform module sequencing (owner: Liam) -- separate infra-only changes from control-plane changes. Plan the TF changes in three logical waves: (A) infra idempotency/fixes (no service restart), (B) control-plane resource changes (ConfigMaps, secrets rotation), (C) runtime node IAM/taint/label changes that force drain/recreate. Provide exact terraform plan examples and the expected diff hunks.

4) Runtime rollout strategy -- small canary (1-3 nodes) -> regional expansion -> global. Canary workloads must run synthetic trace workloads (see test harness links) and user-sim traffic with 10x QPS for stress. For canaries, run both old and new runtimes behind split traffic via service mesh + header routing.

5) API/CRD compatibility guardrails -- keep CRD webhook validation additive only. If a new required field is introduced, ship a short-lived admission webhook fallback that backfills defaults. Maintain backwards compatibility for get/list/watch semantics. Document every API version bump in release notes and add a forced in-cluster flag to enable new fields per-namespace.

6) KV schema & cache migration -- never migrate live KV across formats without dual-read support. Technique: write-as-new-version, read fallback to old version, run background reconciler to backfill. Invalidate runtime prefix caches via coordinated TTL bump and explicit prefix eviction calls.

7) Canary validation metrics & thresholds -- define pass/fail: 99th pct latency delta <= 20% vs baseline, error rate increase < 0.1%, CPU/GPU utilization within expected bounds, token throughput per second within +/-15%. If any gate fails, abort rollout and trigger automated rollback.

8) Rollback procedures -- two rollback types: fast rollback (revert control-plane routing + runtime image roll back) and stateful rollback (requires KV reconciliation and potentially DB migration reversal). Always prefer fast rollback to restore availability, then plan a follow-up for stateful recovery offline.

9) Terraform state considerations -- never perform module refactor that renames resources during a live cutover. If name changes required, use import/migrate pattern in a maintenance window with explicit owner and double-checked state backups.

10) Rehearsal run (lab cluster) -- run full upgrade runbook in lab that simulates slow disks, SLO-violating traffic patterns, and partial failure scenarios (control plane unavailable, node drain failing). Record timings and operator runbook steps.

11) Communication & runbook play actions -- pre-upgrade notice to customers (72h), maintenance window expectation, Slack/Pager duty rotation, dedicated channel, Ops lead to run canary and confirm metrics, Product/Support to stand-by for customer inquiries.

12) Post-upgrade smoke tests & regression sweep -- run integration tests, evals on sample prompt set for quality regressions, and cost-per-token sampling. Automate alerts for semantic drift in outputs for 24h post-upgrade.

13) After-action & roll-forward cadence -- collect timeline, what went well/poorly, update terraform module docs, mark tickets for follow-ups (e.g., longer-term API simplification).
checklist:
- [ ] Inventory CSV uploaded to JIRA
- [ ] Compatibility matrix reviewed by runtime+control-plane leads
- [ ] Terraform plan examples validated in staging
- [ ] Lab rehearsal completed and recorded
- [ ] Canary test harness configured and thresholds set
- [ ] Customer comms drafted and scheduled
- [ ] Rollback artifacts validated (state snapshots, image tags)
- [ ] Post-upgrade eval set ready
unresolved_questions:
- Do we want to permit 'delta' TF module changes (minor field rename) during canary? (pros: faster fixes; cons: complex state manipulation)
- For operator CRD gating, should we prefer feature flags over admission webhooks?
- How long do we retain dual-read compatibility for KV schema before we hard-cut?
notes_to_self: Keep playbook short and prescriptive — teams will ignore long prose during incident. Capture exact CLI commands for drain/import/evict in the final runbook. Record exact metric queries (PromQL) for canary validation. Schedule a dry-run with Solutions Eng before customer cutovers.

final_note: This remains a draft. Next steps: align with SRE and platform-eng, lock down owner list, and produce a short 'operator cheat sheet' with the 10 most used commands. Intended audience: engineers running private deployments and solutions engineers coordinating cutovers.
